  -> integrate(-1 / (2 * (x + 1)) + 1 / (2 * (x - 1)), x)
  Verified by symbolic equivalence: Combining the partial fractions recovers the original fraction.
  Partial-fraction identity: 1 / (x ^ 2 - 1) = -1 / (2 * (x + 1)) + 1 / (2 * (x - 1))
Step 2 (Integrate each partial fraction): Integrate the separated terms. Each linear denominator contributes a logarithm of an absolute value, while the remaining power and quadratic terms use their elementary rules.
  integrate(-1 / (2 * (x + 1)) + 1 / (2 * (x - 1)), x)
  -> -log(abs(x + 1)) / 2 + log(abs(x - 1)) / 2 + C
  Verified by differentiation: Differentiating the final result recovers the rational function on every interval where the original denominator is nonzero.
  Term 1: integrate(-1 / (2 * (x + 1)), x) = -log(abs(x + 1)) / 2
  Term 2: integrate(1 / (2 * (x - 1)), x) = log(abs(x - 1)) / 2
  Domain constraint: x != -1 (The original denominator cannot equal zero.)
